Subject: Patch windows & service-credit adjustments — initial redline

Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We reviewed the MSA + Order Form and attached a redline that tightens availability carveouts around patching. Two asks from our side:

- Define "emergency patch" and limit planned patch windows to no more than 4 hours per week (we understand some weeks may be heavier).
- If patching causes >0.05% additional downtime in the monthly uptime calculation, we'd like a proportional credit (we proposed a stepped ladder in the attached doc).

We left the response-time tiers as-is but proposed tightening the P1 acknowledgement window to 15 minutes (currently 30). Please confirm if Redwood ops can commit to that for Dedicated customers, or if there needs to be an SLA exception with an alternative credit schedule.

Attached: ByteWave_Redlines_v3.docx

Looking for a quick yes/no on the emergency/weekly patch cap and whether you want us to convert the redline into tracked changes in the DocuSign package.

Thanks,
Samir
Procurement Manager, ByteWave

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Patch windows & service-credit adjustments — initial redline

Samir — thanks for the detailed notes and the redline. We're aligned on the goal here: minimize surprise downtime from maintenance while keeping the ability to push critical fixes. Quick replies to your asks: 

- "Emergency patch": ops definition matters — typically for us that means a CVE with active exploitation or a production-impacting failure. Lauren (legal) flagged that we should add objective triggers to avoid ambiguity.
- Patch cadence: I hear the ask for a 4-hour/week cap. I'll loop in Ops (Connor) to get a technical feasibility commitment for Dedicated customers, and ops will propose acceptable blackout and schedule notice windows.
- P1 ack window: 15 minutes is tight but reasonable for Dedicated with a 24/7 on-call; we need confirmation from Ops and possibly a class-based exception in the Order Form if ByteWave needs reduced credits in exchange.

I've uploaded a short spreadsheet that maps your proposed credit ladder to our current calculation so we can see dollar impact: redline-summary.xlsx (attached).

Next steps I propose: Ops & Legal + a short 30-min sync with you to finalize the definition and agree on a credit cap/cap floor. If that works, we'll prepare a DocuSign package with tracked changes. When are you available Mon/Tue next week?

—Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Patch windows & service-credit adjustments — legal comments

Forwarding my inline notes on ByteWave_Redlines_v3.docx — see below for the main legal positions.

On Thu, 11 Jan 2028 at 09:12, Samir Shah <samir.shah@bytewave.io> wrote:
> Marissa,
>
> Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday...

Lauren's summary (high level):

1) Emergency patch definition: propose a three-prong test — (a) active, exploitable vulnerability; (b) imminent data-loss or P1 degradation; or (c) regulatory requirement requiring immediate remediation. This provides objective triggers and avoids subjective "emergency" disputes.

2) Patch window cap: legal is OK to accept a mutually-agreed weekly cap for scheduled patches provided: (i) Redwood gives >=48 hours written notice for scheduled windows; (ii) emergency patch exceptions are explicitly listed; and (iii) there's a hard annual cap on scheduled maintenance hours (to avoid unconstrained weekly stacking).

3) Credit ladder: recommend a capped proportional credit with a monthly floor. We propose: credits accrue per outage minute attributable to maintenance beyond the agreed baseline, but total monthly credits cannot exceed the lesser of (a) 50% of monthly fees for the impacted service, or (b) the aggregate cap in the Order Form. This keeps vendor liability bounded.

4) P1 ack: legal prefers to keep acknowledgement and time-to-resolution separate. We're fine acknowledging at 15 minutes if Ops guarantees an on-call who will triage immediately; otherwise, propose a 30-minute ack with an accelerated remediation SLA for Dedicated.

Please see attached Doc (redline v3) for tracked language. Connor — please weigh in on the practicality of the notice windows and annual cap: can Redwood commit to 48-hour notice for scheduled patch windows and to a yearly maximum?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Samir / Emily — thanks everyone for the quick turn. Short summary and proposed path forward: 

- Definition: Agree to Lauren's three-prong emergency definition; we will insert that language into the Order Form.
- Notice: Connor confirms (below) that 48 hours notice for scheduled patch windows is operationally feasible for Dedicated; we'll catalogue emergency exceptions in the Order Form.
- Annual cap: Ops suggests an annual scheduled-maintenance cap of 208 hours (4 hours/week average) with language that allows exceptions for security remediations that meet the emergency definition.
- Credits: Legal's capped-ladder approach looks fair — we'll model dollar exposure in the attached spreadsheet and propose a cap equal to 50% of monthly fees or the Order Form aggregate, whichever is lower.

Next steps: 
1) Quick sync (30 min) to lock final wording — propose Tue 2028-01-17 10:00 PT.
2) I'll prepare a DocuSign package with tracked changes after the call.
3) If you want faster progress, accept the DocuSign prep link and we can pre-seed the redline.

Connor / Jonas — could you both confirm the 48-hour notice + annual cap feasibility in a one-liner reply so we can send timing to Samir?
